boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a dated notice, בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ם בֶּן יֹאושִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔ה מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte), matching “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.27.1) — naming Jehoiakim in the defective spelling the bytes actually carry, not a fuller alternative. A command to wear a sign follows at once, on the command's own bare messenger formula, כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.27.2, byte), addressed to the prophet himself rather than through him to a third party, then עֲשֵׂ֣ה לְךָ֔ מוֹסֵר֖וֹת וּמֹט֑וֹת וּנְתַתָּ֖ם עַל צַוָּארֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.27.2, byte), matching “Make bonds and bars, and put them on your neck.” (web:Jer.27.2). The envoys the sign is sent through are said to come יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.27.3, byte), matching “to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.27.3): the reign named at the header and the reign the delivered sign actually reaches diverge, and that divergence is held open here rather than resolved by reading a different king at the header. A single relayed message follows without any change of speaker, opening on the full title stack כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.27.4, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says” (web:Jer.27.4); nothing inside verses 5 through 10 reopens that stack with a different speaker or turns to a different addressee. A second-person plural directive does stand inside that stretch, וְ֠אַתֶּם אַל תִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֶל נְבִיאֵיכֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.27.9, byte), matching “But as for you, don’t listen to your prophets,” (web:Jer.27.9), but it does not cut a fresh unit here: its addressee is the same royal audience the relayed message has spoken to since verse 4, not a newly introduced one. It closes on וְהַגּ֗וֹי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֧יא אֶת צַוָּאר֛וֹ בְּעֹ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וַֽעֲבָד֑וֹ וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte), matching “But the nation that brings their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, that nation I will let remain in their own land,’ says Yahweh;” (web:Jer.27.11). Verse 12 opens a fresh address, וְאֶל צִדְקִיָּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.27.12, byte) — from the envoys of five foreign kings to Zedekiah named directly in Jeremiah’s own first-person report — and this row stops short of that turn.

boundary_rationale: A fresh dated notice opens the unit and a new scene, standing mid-verse rather than verse-initially — unlike the accession header at 27:1, this one follows a vayehi-bashanah-hahi opening, וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte), as its own fourth and fifth words (sweep: this spelling stands in 2 verses, 27:1 and 28:1; the two-spelling class stands in 3, adding the byform at 26:1) — וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה בשנת בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִעִ֔ית בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֑י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֡י חֲנַנְיָה֩ בֶן עַזּ֨וּר הַנָּבִ֜יא אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִגִּבְעוֹן֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֧י הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte), matching “That same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah the son of Azzur, the prophet, who was of Gibeon, spoke to me in Yahweh’s house, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.28.1) — the named prophet entering the scene, Hananiah son of Azzur. A ketiv/qere note sits inside this same opening verse, on the year-phrase itself: ketiv בשנת against qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ (oshb:Jer.28.1, WLC, single-witness). Hananiah’s own speech follows without a break, carrying the full divine formula in a false prophet’s mouth: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁבַ֞רְתִּי אֶת עֹ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.28.2, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, ‘I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.” (web:Jer.28.2) — the formula here names Hananiah as its speaker, not Yahweh directly, and that mouth is disclosed rather than left to the digit alone. The same quoted speech closes on וְאֶת יְכָנְיָ֣ה בֶן יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְ֠הוּדָה וְאֶת כָּל גָּל֨וּת יְהוּדָ֜ה הַבָּאִ֣ים בָּבֶ֗לָה אֲנִ֥י מֵשִׁ֛יב אֶל הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.4, byte), matching “I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, who went to Babylon,’ says Yahweh;” (web:Jer.28.4) — the closing formula belongs to the same mouth named two verses earlier, Hananiah’s own, not Yahweh’s. A new speaker answers him by name at verse 5, so this row goes no further.

Plant gardens and eat their fruit.” (web:Jer.29.5). boundary_rationale: A cataphoric summons back to the letter’s own audience opens the unit, וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר שִׁלַּ֥חְתִּי מִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.29.20, byte), matching “Hear therefore Yahweh’s word, all you captives whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.” (web:Jer.29.20) — the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative naming the exiles, its own count object standing in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier), read here as belonging forward with the oracle it introduces rather than backward as the close of the Jerusalem judgment it follows.
